content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad with Italian dressing is a classic side dish made from boiled potatoes cut into cubes, mixed with vegetables such as onion, bell pepper, and tomato, and tossed in a dressing of olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, herbs and spices typical of Italian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Italian dressing often includes oregano, basil, and garlic, giving the salad a bright aroma.
In Italy, potato salad is traditionally served cold as an appetizer alongside main courses.
Italian versions may add capers or olives for extra flavor.
The salad keeps its taste for several hours in the fridge but is best eaten within 24 hours.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vegetables and lemon juice in the dressing provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Olive oil supplies monounsaturated fats that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Potassium for blood pressure regulation
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, helping maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Potatoes and added vegetables contribute dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Herbs such as basil and oregano contain antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to olive oil, oregano, or other spices used in the dressing.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Adding too much salt can make the dish unsuitable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: Improper storage at room temperature for more than 2 hours may allow bacterial proliferation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a side or a standalone snack. It can be added to sandwiches, used as a filling for wraps, or paired with grilled meats.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Stir before serving, as the dressing may settle.
